One fish. Mark the dark region in Tank area tools. Any usable tank area outside marked regions is light; masked and uncertain positions are unknown.

Every 0.2 seconds · 5 samples/sec

Advanced settings

Requires changes beyond the usual brightness range of each pixel, reducing flickering ridges and fixtures. Fish can still cross these areas. Turn off if faint fish are missed. Fixed bright details are already part of the background.

Use intervals of 250 ms or less. T numbers follow provisional paths; identities can swap during overlap. Dashed † centers are uncertain estimates. With the center rule below, recent paths can help separate an overlap for up to one second after a clear observation.

With one fish expected, background detection keeps the strongest foreground contrast instead of weaker reflections. Similar candidates remain uncertain; review the pink × marks and correct the center when needed.

Optional: only discard candidates when the count exceeds the known fish count. Pink × marks show excluded candidates. A real fish at the edge can also be excluded; check the choices in Results. Touching fish are checked before this rule chooses the nearest candidates. Splits can use two visible dark bodies or the preceding observed sample (up to 250 ms apart); † centers remain estimates. The center is the middle of the crop rectangle.

Works best with a fixed camera. Include the fish’s swimming area, then mask wall reflections. Fewer blobs than the known count may mean missed or overlapping fish; extra blobs may come from tank edges or reflections.

Model settings Roboflow InferenceJS

Using zebrafish_in_aquarium/9, a trained YOLOv8n model for zebrafish. Enter a Roboflow workspace publishable key, never a private API key.

Calibrate from a known length

Draw along a known distance in the preview, enter its length in inches, then use the scale.

Measure several grid squares near the swimming area for better accuracy. Perspective makes distances approximate. Clearing the line keeps the applied scale.

For a light/dark tank, select Mark dark region and outline the dark side, then Mark light region and outline the light side. Use Four corners for angled areas: click four corners in order around the edge. This also works for the tank crop and reflection masks. Marked regions keep fish in the analysis; reflection masks exclude them. Dark regions detect brighter or darker fish; light and unmarked regions detect darker fish. The last region drawn wins at overlaps. With one fish expected and a marked dark region, the rest of the usable tank counts as light and the timeline tracks side changes. Other recordings report centers outside marked regions as unmarked. Analyze again after changes.

Precise crop

Four-corner tank selections analyze only the outlined area; precise crop fields below replace that outline with a rectangle. Masks exclude reflections and any real fish that enter those areas. Changing the crop or masks requires analyzing again.

Diagnostics: fish & reflections

Higher S usually means sharper edges. Scores are not probabilities or a 0–100 scale. Grid lines, contrast, noise, and motion can affect them. Compare candidates from the same recording.

# is a candidate ID within this frame; group numbers are separate. * means the scoring patch was clipped by the crop or a mask. “—” means too few pixels or no usable box. † marks an uncertain overlap estimate. T numbers identify provisional paths across frames, not verified fish identities; check estimates against neighboring frames.

Label candidates as fish or reflections to compare their scores across frames. Labels stay in this tab until results are cleared or the tab reloads; export them to keep them. Labels do not filter detections. Pink × marks identify excluded candidates. The table distinguishes weaker contrast, ambiguous single-fish choices, and outer candidates.

How metrics work

Each detection center is a candidate fish position. Centers within the link distance form connected groups; a chain of links can join fish farther apart. Single fish are shown separately. The random comparison places the same number of points uniformly inside the selected tank crop, excluding reflection masks, 399 times and compares mean nearest-neighbor distance. A low percentile means tighter spacing than those random placements in that frame; adjacent video frames are not independent tests. Inch estimates use the paper-grid calibration and are approximate. When the detected count is low, the detector checks close to the crop edge, then may split a large joined region. These estimates are marked in the raw export. Reflections can create extras. Background tracking follows provisional paths across nearby frames; dashed † positions are uncertain and need review. Read the full method.

Choose a fish button to select an overlapping box. In Move or resize mode, drag inside a box to move it or drag a corner to resize it. Width and height also adjust the selected box. Editing a labeled frame makes it a draft until you mark it labeled again.

Choose training frames

You can skip any frames. Only explicitly labeled frames enter the dataset. Label an empty frame only when it contains no real fish. Arrow keys navigate; L toggles labeled status when you are not typing in a control.

Dataset ZIP: clean cropped PNGs, YOLO boxes, and a JSON annotation manifest. Skipped and draft frames are excluded. Save progress JSON includes drafts and images for resuming with this video, crop, and interval; restoring it replaces this labeling project's current marks.

Review buttons explained

Use Done & next for each frame. It applies any pending edits, updates the summary, marks the frame done, and advances. If the frame is already correct, it just marks it done and advances.

Main actions
ButtonWhat it does
Done & nextApplies pending corrections and marks this frame done, then advances. At the end, it returns to any unfinished frames in this view or shows review complete.
Apply & stayApplies pending corrections, updates the summary, and marks the frame done while keeping it on screen. Available when there are unapplied edits.
Download frame PNGSaves the selected video image at its original resolution. It uses the current crop or full-frame view and leaves out drawn centers and overlays.
Editing controls
ControlWhat it does
Edit centersEnables editing, starting from the current detections or your existing draft. Stays enabled as you apply corrections and move between frames.
Undo markUndoes the last draft edit. Use Done & next or Apply & stay to update results.
Start from current centersReplaces your draft with the centers currently used in results.
Clear draft centersEmpties the draft. Applying an empty draft sets this frame’s fish count to zero.
Restore automatic centersRestores the original detections and resets the draft to them. Undo mark can recover the previous draft.

Previous/Next and the arrow keys navigate without applying drafts. Fit / − / + only change the view.

Progress above the summary shows how many frames are done in the current view. When it says Review complete, export results to keep your work. Editing a completed frame makes it unfinished again.
